title: Kirtan Sohila at night
hookLine: five short hymns said before sleep

cards: What's the last thing you do before you fall asleep? For a lot of people, honestly, it's the phone: one more scroll, one more video, the blue light on the ceiling. Then sleep comes thin.
Parents know a better way from the other side. A child's bedtime has a ritual: the bath, the story, the song, the light going off. The same song every night, so the child knows it's safe to let go.
Sikhs have a bedtime song of their own.

teach.b: Kirtan Sohila is short: five hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib, three by Guru Nanak, one by Guru Ram Das, one by Guru Arjan. It's the last bani of the Sikh day, said at night before sleep.
Sohila means a song of praise, and in Punjab it's also a word for wedding songs. That's a clue. Guru Nanak's first hymn uses wedding pictures.
In paraphrase: in the house where the Creator's praises are sung, sing the song of praise and remember the Creator.
Then comes a bride whose wedding day has been set, and friends pouring oil on the threshold, the old custom for welcoming a bride, asked to bless her so she may meet her Lord. The bride is the soul.
The wedding is the meeting with God. And here's what makes Sohila unusual: that wedding also means death.
Sikhs read Kirtan Sohila every night, and at funerals, after a cremation. The same song for sleep and for death. It isn't meant to be grim.
Sleep is a small letting go every night. The Gurus picture death, the great letting go, as a wedding day, not a door slamming.
Saying Sohila at night rehearses trust: whatever the night holds, the soul is not going somewhere cold.
Another of Guru Nanak's hymns in Sohila pictures the whole sky as a platter for God's worship: sun and moon the lamps, the stars the pearls. You're lying down under that sky tonight.

how: Sikhs recite Kirtan Sohila at night before sleep as the last bani of Nitnem; it is also read at funerals after cremation, and when the Guru Granth Sahib is closed for the night in the gurdwara.

a lullaby sung only to small children

games.q: Sohila's first hymn pictures a wedding day that's been fixed. what does the day stand for?
o: a real wedding the Guru attended.
the soul's meeting with God, which is also death.
the start of a new year.
games.why: the bride is the soul and the wedding is the meeting with God. that's why Sohila is said at funerals, and every night before sleep.

practice: If you can, listen to the first hymn of Kirtan Sohila; it takes about a minute. If not, close your eyes and picture tonight: the phone face down across the room, the lights off, moon and stars outside the window.
If you pray, let Sohila's first line be there; if not, just let go, the way a child does when the song ends.

wordCard.voice: Sohila. A song of praise, and a wedding song: five hymns Sikhs say at night, and at funerals too.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sohila, a song of praise; also a wedding song.

carryVoice: Your line: the night song. A wedding song, sung at the edge of sleep. Sleep well; see you tomorrow.
